scenes.headline: How SPACE gives every agent task its own VM
scenes.sub: A jailed microVM per task, and a gateway that holds the keys.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Toggle! These agents get root inside a sandbox. Here is how the host and the keys stay out of reach.

scenes.text: Give each task a small virtual machine, and handle its network and credentials from outside the machine, where the agent cannot reach.
scenes.say: The idea. Each task gets a small virtual machine, and its network and keys are handled from outside it.

scenes.title: What an escape has to get through

steps.say: The agent has root, but only over a guest kernel that nothing else depends on.
Below it, Firecracker runs in a jail, with its own user and namespaces and hard resource limits.
Only then the hardware boundary and the host.
Every connection from the guest goes to a gateway that serves only this sandbox, on the host.
It checks the policy. Metadata and private ranges are always denied.
If a rule's host, path and method match, the gateway adds the key on the way out. The guest never sees it.

items.say: Running: live memory and a copy-on-write disk.
Paused: memory stays on the worker. Fast, not durable.
Suspended: dirty memory and changed disk go to storage.
Forked: frozen, captured, restored as a new sandbox.

steps.say: Then they attacked it. Nine model setups with root tried for a host secret. No escape in one hundred and eight runs.
With some network allowed, agents slipped past the egress rules in eleven of fifty four runs, before the fix.

scenes.label: upper bound on the escape rate, from 0 of 108
scenes.note: independent runs assumed; these attackers only
scenes.say: Zero of one hundred and eight is not a proof. Generously, it bounds the rate near three percent.

scenes.text: A microVM guards the host. The network and the keys are a separate boundary, and that is the one that broke.
scenes.say: The takeaway. The machine guards the host. The network and keys are a separate boundary, and that one broke.
To recap. One jailed machine per task, keys attached outside, and sandboxes that pause, suspend and fork.
